name: enzyme
description: The enzyme used for peptide digestion.

name: decoys
description: Decoy handling for target-decoy FDR. 'auto': ensure decoys are available — reuse decoys already present in the database (marker auto-detected, prefix or suffix) or generate them if none are found. Supplied decoys are reused only at 0.5 to 2 decoys per target protein: target-decoy FDR needs about one decoy per target, so a database with far fewer or more is refused (use 'generate'). 'generate': always (re)generate decoys from the target proteins (any pre-existing decoys are removed first to avoid decoy-of-decoy entries). 'ignore': search the target proteins only — any decoys present in the database are removed.

name: decoy_prefix
description: Accession prefix prepended to decoy proteins when ProSE generates them (modes 'auto' without existing decoys, and 'generate'). Pre-existing decoys in the database are detected automatically (any common marker, used as prefix or suffix) and do not require this setting.

name: decoy_method
description: How ProSE generates decoys (decoys 'generate', or 'auto' with a database without decoys). 'reverse' (ProSEAlgorithm's default; the ProSE tool's default is 'keep_termini'): every enzymatic segment of the protein is reversed except its last residue (the last segment entirely), an initial Met stays first with peptide:clip_nterm_methionine. 'keep_termini': the construction of OpenMS DecoyDatabase (method reverse, Decoy:keepPeptideNTerm/keepPeptideCTerm true) with the search enzyme and Decoy:non_shuffle_pattern 'KRP': in every segment of a digest without missed cleavages, the first and the last residue and every K, R and P stay in place and the rest is reversed. For enzymes whose cleavage sites are fixed by these residues (Trypsin, Trypsin/P, Lys-C, Arg-C and the like) every target peptide then has a decoy with the same start, length, mass and cleavage sites: also every protein N-terminal and Met-clipped one, so that peptide:clip_nterm_methionine and protein N-terminal modifications add the same number of target and decoy candidates (except peptides that equal their decoy, e.g. made of short segments or of K, R and P only; and modifications specific to a peptide's first residue, e.g. pyro-Glu on an N-terminal Q, apply to the target and its decoy alike only where that residue is kept in place). Semi- or non-specific digestion: as 'reverse'. Other enzymes: a warning names the decoys whose cleavage sites differ from the target's. No effect on decoys taken from the database (decoys 'auto' with decoys in it). The results differ from 'reverse'.

name: low_memory
description: Non-specific searches (peptide:enzyme_specificity=none; ignored otherwise): index the peptide masses, as the prefixes of one mother peptide per protein position, instead of the fragments of every peptidoform, and generate the fragments of the peptidoforms in the precursor window at query time. Finds the same candidates with a fraction of the memory (e.g. for immunopeptidomics against a human database), but takes more time per spectrum, the more the wider the precursor window.

name: precursor:mass_tolerance_lower
description: Lower-side precursor-mass tolerance (positive magnitude; effective window is [-lower, +upper] around the precursor). When strongly asymmetric, also review precursor:isotope_error_min.

name: precursor:mass_tolerance_upper
description: Upper-side precursor-mass tolerance (positive magnitude).

name: precursor:mass_tolerance_unit
description: Unit of precursor mass tolerance.

name: precursor:min_charge
description: Minimum precursor charge to be considered. Spectra without a precursor charge are searched with every charge of the range; spectra whose recorded charge lies outside of it are searched at that charge, or not at all with precursor:recorded_charge_outside_range 'skip'.

name: precursor:max_charge
description: Maximum precursor charge to be considered (see precursor:min_charge).

name: precursor:recorded_charge_outside_range
description: A spectrum whose recorded precursor charge lies outside of precursor:min_charge..max_charge: 'skip' (the default, as OpenMS develop since #10713) does not search it; 'search' (the behaviour before #10713) searches it at its recorded charge, up to charge 20. Spectra without a recorded charge are searched with every charge of the range.

name: precursor:isotope_error_min
description: Minimum precursor isotope error searched, in 13C spacings (1.00336 Da) added to the observed precursor mass: -1 finds a peptide whose first 13C isotope peak was selected as the precursor. The PSM meta value 'isotope_error' reports the opposite sign by default (see report:isotope_error_convention).

name: precursor:isotope_error_max
description: Maximum precursor isotope error searched, with the sign of precursor:isotope_error_min: +1 finds a peptide whose precursor was selected one 13C spacing below its monoisotopic peak.

name: fragment:mass_tolerance
description: Fragment mass tolerance

name: fragment:mass_tolerance_unit
description: Unit of fragment m

name: fragment:deisotope
description: MS2 deisotoping (single-charge deconvolution) before searching. 'auto' deisotopes only when the fragment tolerance is within the high-resolution deisotoper range (<= 0.1 Da / <= 100 ppm) and skips it for low-resolution (e.g. ion-trap CID) data; 'true' always deisotopes (requires a high-resolution fragment tolerance); 'false' never deisotopes.

name: fragment:deisotope_min_peaks
description: Minimum number of peaks, the monoisotopic peak included, of an isotope envelope that MS2 deisotoping collapses into its monoisotopic peak. With 2 (Sage-like), an ion whose M+2 peak is lost in the noise loses its M+1 peak too, so the M+1 peak no longer takes a place in the per-window peak quota, and a multiply charged ion seen with two isotope peaks is converted to charge 1; in dense spectra (e.g. timsTOF) more of the two-peak multiply charged envelopes are chance pairs. 3 is the earlier behaviour.

name: fragment:deisotope_charge_cap
description: Fragment charges that MS2 deisotoping tries. 'precursor' tries charges up to the precursor charge, but at most 3 (1-3 when the precursor charge is unknown): a fragment cannot carry more charges than its precursor, so a chance peak 1/3 Th above an ion of a 2+ precursor cannot turn the ion into a '3+' envelope at a wrong m/z. This is Sage-like; Sage caps at the precursor charge without the limit of 3 and counts an unknown charge as 3. 'none' tries charges 1-3 in every spectrum (the earlier behaviour).

name: fragment:deisotope_sum_intensity
description: Give the monoisotopic peak of each isotope envelope the summed intensity of the envelope (Sage-like). 'false' keeps the monoisotopic peak's own intensity (the earlier behaviour).

name: fragment:min_mz
description: Minimal fragment mz for database

name: fragment:max_mz
description: Maximal fragment mz for database

name: fragment:min_ion_index
description: Ions with index less than or equal to this value are not added to the fragment index (use 0 to include all ions; 2 skips b1/b2/y1/y2). Low-index ions are often noisy and unreliable.

name: fragment:query_spectrum
description: Spectrum used for candidate retrieval. 'raw' queries the fragment index with all positive-intensity peaks, before deisotoping and local/top-N filtering, so that spectra whose matching fragments are not among the retained peaks still get candidates; it costs an additional peak list per spectrum and more fragment matches. 'processed' queries with the scoring peak list. 'auto' uses 'raw' for high-resolution fragments (<= 0.1 Da / <= 100 ppm) and 'processed' otherwise: at low resolution, the unfiltered peaks match many random fragments and crowd out the correct candidates. Scoring always uses the processed spectrum.

name: fragment:min_matched_ions
description: Minimal number of matched ions to report a PSM

name: fragment:max_charge
description: max fragment charge

name: peaks:keep_n
description: Maximum number of MS2 peaks kept per spectrum (NLargest) before scoring. 0 = auto: a resolution-aware cap (~400 for high-res, ~80 at 0.5 Da, floor 60) that avoids the spurious low-resolution fragment matching which otherwise inflates HyperScore for targets and decoys alike. Set an explicit value to override (e.g. 400 for the legacy behavior).

name: peaks:window_top
description: Maximum number of MS2 peaks kept per 100 Da window (WindowMower) before scoring.

name: peaks:window_type
description: Local peak filtering. 'auto' uses jump_full for high-resolution fragments (<= 0.1 Da / <= 100 ppm), preserving the strongest peaks even in a short final 100 Da window, and legacy jump filtering otherwise. 'jump' scales the last window's peak quota by its observed width; 'jump_full' keeps the full quota in every window.

name: modifications:fixed
description: Fixed modifications, specified using UniMod (www.unimod.org) terms, e.g. 'Carbamidomethyl (C)'

name: modifications:variable
description: Variable modifications, specified using UniMod (www.unimod.org) terms, e.g. 'Oxidation (M)'. A terminus and a residue carry one modification each: a variable terminal modification (e.g. 'Acetyl (Protein N-term)', 'Gln->pyro-Glu (N-term Q)') is not searched where a fixed one sits on that terminus (e.g. 'TMT6plex (N-term)'), and a variable residue modification (e.g. 'Glutathione (C)') is not searched where a fixed one sits on that residue (e.g. 'Carbamidomethyl (C)').

name: modifications:variable_max_per_peptide
description: Maximum number of residues carrying a variable modification per candidate peptide

name: annotate:PSM
description: Annotations added to each PSM.

name: annotate:self_trained_ion_priors
description: Learn per-run fragment ion likelihoods from the confident PSMs of each file and add the Percolator features of annotate:ion_prior_features to every hit. The spectra are split into two halves by scan parity. Each half trains a model on its rank-one target hits at target-decoy competition q <= annotate:ion_prior_train_fdr of the native score (their reversed sequences on the same spectra are the noise model), and every hit is scored by the model of the other half, so no PSM is scored by a model that saw its spectrum or its label. Needs annotate:ion_prior_min_psms training PSMs in each half, otherwise the features are 0. Not applied to target-only searches (decoys=ignore), which get no features. Native scores and candidate selection are unchanged. Independent of annotate:PSM.

name: annotate:ion_prior_model
description: Contexts and outcomes of the ion priors. Both keep the ion series a/b, x/y, c and z apart (c and z ions are scored for electron-activated spectra, see ions:by_activation). 'rich': ion series, precursor charge, fragment charge, relative position, the residues at the cleavage site (bond before P, bond after D or E) and whether the complementary singly charged ion matched; outcome: intensity rank x mass error (|error| / tolerance below 0.25, below 0.5, up to 1). 'basic': ion series, precursor charge, fragment charge and relative position; outcome: intensity rank.

name: annotate:ion_prior_peaks
description: Peaks the ion priors rank and match. 'all': every peak after deisotoping, before the peaks:window_top and peaks:keep_n filters, so weak fragment ions count as evidence for the model without entering HyperScore. 'scored': the peaks that are scored.

name: annotate:ion_prior_max_fragment_charge
description: Highest fragment charge of the ions of the ion priors; capped at the precursor charge - 1 (at least 1).

name: annotate:ion_prior_train_fdr
description: Target-decoy competition q-value threshold selecting the training PSMs of annotate:self_trained_ion_priors.

name: annotate:ion_prior_min_psms
description: Minimum number of training PSMs of annotate:self_trained_ion_priors in each half of the spectra; with fewer, the features are 0.

name: annotate:ion_prior_features
description: Features of annotate:self_trained_ion_priors written to every hit and listed for Percolator: ion_prior_llr (summed log-likelihood ratio of the ion outcomes, signal vs reversed noise), ion_prior_explained (share of the predicted ion presence that was observed), ion_prior_topk_observed (share of the 6 ions most likely present that were observed).

name: annotate:local_fragment_evidence
description: Add chance_match_surprise and mass_competition_evidence annotations and Percolator features. Uses local peak density and alternative intact/neutral-loss fragment assignments. Retains an additional peak list before window/top-N filtering, increasing memory use. Does not change native scores or candidate selection. Independent of annotate:PSM.

name: peptdeep:instrument
description: Instrument class passed to the PeptDeep MS2 model. An instrument that is not in this list is best approximated by the closest one that is.

name: peptdeep:nce
description: Normalised collision energy for the PeptDeep MS2 model. Negative selects it automatically from the collision energy recorded in the spectra, refined by scoring a small grid on confident PSMs.

name: peptdeep:rt_model_type
description: Model mapping predicted onto observed retention time.

name: peptdeep:batch_size
description: Peptides per ONNX inference call. The calls run side by side, one per thread: small ones keep the threads evenly busy and the memory low (on iPRG2015 with 16 threads, 64 took 40% less time than 500 and 1 GB less memory).

name: peptide:min_size
description: Minimum size a peptide must have after digestion to be considered in the search.

name: peptide:max_size
description: Maximum size a peptide must have after digestion to be considered in the search (0 = disabled).

name: peptide:missed_cleavages
description: Number of missed cleavages.

name: peptide:clip_nterm_methionine
description: Also search protein N-terminal peptides after removal of their initial methionine. The retained-M form is still searched; length, mass and missed-cleavage limits apply to each form. Set false for the previous search space.

name: peptide:deduplicate
description: Index each exact peptidoform once before candidate selection. Protein mappings still list every protein occurrence. Across database chunks, count each peptide/charge/isotope hypothesis once; retaining queried keys adds memory per spectrum. With low_memory, the repeated peptidoforms among the candidates of a spectrum are dropped instead. Set false for occurrence-based legacy candidates.

name: peptide:protein_mapping
description: How the hits are mapped to their proteins (peptide evidences, target_decoy, protein_references, protein hits). 'index': from the digest of the fragment index, which holds every protein occurrence of a candidate (with a protein-terminal modification: from a pass over the database for the hits' sequences); the result is that of PeptideIndexing, which runs instead wherever the index cannot reproduce it exactly (e.g. low_memory, a specificity other than full, a chunked database, symbols other than letters or long stretches of ambiguous residues in the database). 'PeptideIndexing': always search every hit in the whole database (Aho-Corasick), as before.

name: peptide:enzyme_specificity
description: Enzyme cleavage specificity required for both peptide termini.#br#  'full' : both termini must be enzyme-specific (canonical, e.g. tryptic).#br#  'semi' : only one terminus needs to be enzyme-specific (semi-tryptic).#br#  'none' : no enzyme constraint at either terminus; every substring of length#br#           [min_size, max_size] is enumerated. Use this for immunopeptidomics#br#           (e.g. HLA peptides 8..12mers). For very large search spaces consider#br#           tightening 'peptide:min_size'/'peptide:max_size'.

name: peptide:motif
description: If set, only peptides whose unmodified sequence (one-letter codes) contains a match of this regular expression are searched, target and decoy peptides alike, e.g. 'N[^P][ST]' for N-glycosylation sequons or 'C' for cysteine-containing peptides; '^' and '$' anchor it to the peptide termini.

name: peptide:min_mass
description: Minimal peptide mass for database

name: peptide:max_mass
description: Maximal peptide mass for database

name: report:top_hits
description: Maximum number of top scoring hits per spectrum that are reported. With 'rescore', only the best hit per spectrum is reported after the rescoring, and the hits that Percolator rescores are set by 'rescoring:top_hits' (report:top_hits then applies to a run that is not rescored and to -out_pin). FDR:PSM > 0 and the protein FDR (FDR:protein > 0) also keep the best hit of each spectrum only, so values above 1 apply with 'rescore' false, FDR:PSM 0 and FDR:protein 0.

name: report:isotope_error_convention
description: Sign of the precursor isotope error reported for each PSM (meta value 'isotope_error', in 13C spacings of 1.00336 Da). 'observed_minus_theoretical': +1 means the observed precursor lies one 13C spacing above the peptide (its first 13C isotope peak was selected), as in MS-GF+, pepXML and Sage; PercolatorInfile and PercolatorAdapter (-out_pin, -percolator_executable) remove the offset from the precursor mass difference with this sign. The search parameters of the result record it as 'isotope_error_convention'. 'theoretical_minus_observed': the opposite sign, as written by earlier ProSE versions (no record in the search parameters); with it the Percolator input doubles the offset in dm/absdm instead of removing it.

name: percolator:max_train_psms
description: With 'rescore': the most PSMs Percolator trains a model on (0: all). Every PSM is scored, also beyond the cap. For a run with more PSMs, Percolator samples the training PSMs by spectrum (see 'rescoring:subset_mode'); for the model of the files of a multi-file search too small for a model of their own (trained on the files rescored on their own), each of these files contributes at most this many divided by the number of input files (reproducible random spectra), so that none dominates. The run log says when the training PSMs were sampled. Searches below the cap are not affected. Until all files of such a search are searched, ProSE keeps their PSMs before the rescoring for that model: all PSMs of the files too small, and of the others only their share (with 0, all PSMs of every file, also with the ProSE tool's -out_pin).

name: rescoring:terminal_features
description: Two more rescoring features: 'protein_nterm' (1 if the peptide occurs at a protein N-terminus) and 'met_clipped' (1 if it occurs only as the Met-clipped protein N-terminal peptide of peptide:clip_nterm_methionine). They let the rescoring learn the different rate of correct matches of these small peptide classes. Use them only with decoys that populate both classes like the targets (decoy_method 'keep_termini'): with decoys that rarely start with M (reversed proteins, reused with decoys 'auto') they would tell targets from decoys, so they are switched off with a warning. The results differ.

name: rescoring:stratum_q_values
description: Also q-values per stratum (meta values 'stratum' and 'stratum_q_value'): the rescored PSMs of protein N-terminal peptides (incl. Met-clipped ones) and the others each get target-decoy competition of their own ((decoys + 1) / targets, as mokapot's grouped confidence). For a list of N-terminal peptides at an FDR, use the stratum q-value; the main score stays the pooled q-value. Needs decoys that populate the N-terminal classes like the targets (decoy_method 'keep_termini'; with reused decoys that rarely start with M it is switched off with a warning). With rescore_method 'reset' the values are computed on RESET's scores (both decoy sets count as decoys with reset:decoys 'two'), not as RESET's estimate.

name: rescoring:peptide_level
description: Also Percolator's peptide-level q-values (default; 'false' leaves them out), as the percolator executable reports peptides (without -U): after the target-decoy competition of the spectra, the best PSM of each peptide (modified sequence) and label competes, and q-values and PEPs are estimated on these peptides. Every rescored hit gets the values of its peptide as meta values 'percolator_peptide_q_value' and 'percolator_peptide_pep'; a list of peptides at an FDR is the target peptides with percolator_peptide_q_value at most that FDR (the distinct peptides of the PSMs at an FDR are not FDR-controlled at the peptide level). The main score stays the PSM-level q-value. Default Percolator rescoring only (not with rescore_method 'reset', which reports RESET:peptide_q_value, nor with rescore_reuse models). Independent of this parameter, every rescored hit gets ProSE's peptide-level q-value 'peptide q-value' (the name FalseDiscoveryRate writes and EntrapmentEvaluator reads), with one peptide definition for each run and for the pooled runs of a multi-file search (the ProSE tool's -out_merged): FalseDiscoveryRate::applyBasicPeptideLevel() (a peptide is an unmodified sequence, whose best PSM competes with its label) on the PSMs' Percolator PEPs, also with rescore_reuse models; not with rescore_method 'reset'.

name: FDR:PSM
description: Filter PSMs based on q-value (e.g., 0.05 = 5% FDR; 0 disables the filter). Target and decoy PSMs are filtered alike by the threshold; decoys that pass are kept (no decoy-specific stripping here — decoys are removed only at protein-FDR finalization). With 'rescore' (the default), the threshold applies to the Percolator q-values, the main score of the rescored PSMs. Without rescoring ('rescore' false, or a run that Percolator did not rescore), 0 computes no q-values: every PSM keeps its search engine score ('ln(hyperscore)') as main score, e.g. as input for Percolator or a downstream FDR step. Above 0, the target-decoy q-value (see FDR:PSM_groups) replaces the main score (the search engine score is kept as meta value 'ln(hyperscore)_score') and only the best hit of each spectrum is kept. If no PSM matched a decoy, the q-value of the T PSMs is the conservative 1/T (target-decoy competition with +1), so a lower threshold reports no PSM instead of lifting the filter. Needs decoys ('decoys' auto or generate); with 'ignore', a threshold above 0 is skipped with a warning (the QPX run view of the ProSE tool's -qpx_extended records per input whether the filter was applied: 'psm_fdr_applied'). Afterwards, the proteins that no remaining PSM references are removed. The final PSM FDR with FDR:protein > 0 (e.g. 0.01), a loose evidence threshold of the intermediates with FDR:protein 0 (e.g. 0.1; see there).

name: FDR:PSM_groups
description: Target-decoy competitions of FDR:PSM. 'pooled' ranks all PSMs together. 'scored_charges' computes q-values separately for PSMs scored with different numbers of fragment charges (scoring:fragment_charges): HyperScore grows with the number of theoretical ions, so when multiply charged fragments are scored for precursors of charge 3 and above but not for charge 2, a pooled competition is dominated by the higher precursor charges. With singly charged fragments only (deisotoped, high-resolution spectra) there is one group, as with 'pooled'. With fragment:max_charge above 2, precursor charges of 4 and above form further groups, which accept few PSMs per run (tens), so their q-values (D/T, as FalseDiscoveryRate) are coarse. A group without decoy or without target PSMs falls back to 'pooled'.

name: FDR:protein
description: Picked-protein FDR threshold (e.g. 0.01 = 1 %), and the switch between the two modes of a search. Above 0, the search is the whole experiment: its proteins are inferred on the pooled PSMs of all its inputs, filtered at this protein FDR, and the PSMs filtered finally, so every output is the final result (the decoys removed, see the ProSE tool's -keep_decoys). With 0 (the default), the search is one part of a larger experiment, e.g. one shard of files searched on one compute node: every output is a per-run intermediate (PSM q-values and PEPs per run, FDR:PSM as a loose evidence threshold, decoys and the proteins the search indexed for the run's PSMs kept), to be finished downstream on all parts together (e.g. ProteomicsLFQ, or IDMerger, ProteinInference or Epifany, FalseDiscoveryRate and IDFilter). Uses the picked-protein approach (Savitski et al. 2015) which pairs target and decoy proteins by accession. The protein inference and the picked-protein FDR use the PSMs up to FDR:protein_inference_PSM, and a protein scores with the best posterior error probability of its PSMs (Percolator's, with 'rescore'; without it the best search engine score). The proteins and the protein groups (which have q-values of their own) are filtered at the threshold, and only the proteins of the groups that pass are kept. Proteins without a reported PSM (one that passes FDR:PSM) are removed afterwards, and so are the PSMs all of whose proteins failed the protein FDR. Needs decoys ('decoys' auto or generate).

name: FDR:protein_inference_PSM
description: q-value cutoff of the PSMs that protein inference and the protein FDR (FDR:protein > 0) use; FDR:PSM still filters the reported PSMs. Without the protein FDR it has no effect. The q-values are those FDR:PSM filters on (Percolator's with 'rescore', else see FDR:PSM_groups). A looser cutoff than FDR:PSM leaves more decoy proteins for the picked-protein FDR, as ProteomicsLFQ infers proteins on PSMs at a looser q-value than its PSM FDR. Values at or below FDR:PSM use the PSMs of FDR:PSM; with FDR:PSM 0 (no PSM filter) all PSMs are used.

name: scoring:max_candidates_per_spectrum
description: The number of initial hits for which we calculate a score

name: scoring:fragment_charges
description: Fragment charges of the theoretical spectra that score each candidate. 'single' scores singly charged fragments only. 'multiple' adds charges up to min(precursor charge - 1, fragment:max_charge). 'auto' uses 'multiple' when the MS2 spectra are not deisotoped (fragment:deisotope=false, or a fragment tolerance above the deisotoper's limit of 0.1 Da / 100 ppm, as for ion-trap CID) and 'single' otherwise, because deisotoping converts fragments to charge 1.

name: scoring:method
description: Native score. 'hyperscore' is the X!Tandem HyperScore. 'mass_accuracy' weights each matched fragment's contribution to HyperScore's ion counts and intensity product by exp(-0.5 * (error / scoring:mass_error_sd)^2), with the error in ppm, so that matches near the theoretical m/z count fully and matches at the edge of the tolerance count little; exact matches score as HyperScore. The kernel is centred at 0 and suits high-resolution fragments only. 'auto' (default) uses 'mass_accuracy' for fragment tolerances in ppm within the high-resolution range (<= 100 ppm) and 'hyperscore' otherwise (Da tolerances, e.g. ion-trap CID). Matching tolerances, candidates and the unweighted match annotations are unchanged. The score type stays 'ln(hyperscore)'; the search parameters record scoring:method_resolved when the weighted score is used.

name: scoring:mass_error_sd
description: Standard deviation in ppm of the Gaussian fragment mass-error kernel of scoring:method 'mass_accuracy'. Fixed (not fitted) and independent of the matching tolerance and of calibration.

name: ions:add_y_ions
description: Add peaks of y-ions to the spectrum

name: ions:add_b_ions
description: Add peaks of b-ions to the spectrum

name: ions:add_a_ions
description: Add peaks of a-ions to the spectrum

name: ions:add_c_ions
description: Add peaks of c-ions to the spectrum

name: ions:add_x_ions
description: Add peaks of  x-ions to the spectrum

name: ions:add_z_ions
description: Add peaks of z-ions (y - NH3) to the spectrum. These are not the z+1 ions of ETD-type spectra; see ions:by_activation and ions:add_zp1_ions.

name: ions:add_zp1_ions
description: Add peaks of z+1 ions (z-dot, y - NH2) to the spectrum, the main C-terminal fragments of ETD, EThcD and ETciD spectra, for all spectra. ions:by_activation adds them (with c ions) for spectra recorded as electron-activated; set this, typically with ions:add_c_ions, for ETD-type data without activation information.

name: ions:by_activation
description: Score spectra whose precursor was activated by electrons (ETD, ECD, EThcD or ETciD, as recorded in the input file) with c and z+1 ions in addition to the ion series above. Other spectra, and spectra without activation information, use the ion series above.

name: calibration:enabled
description: Measure the mass error of the run and search with windows derived from it: a fast calibration pass on the most intense spectra (calibration:subset_ratio), searched with at least 20 ppm (in Da: twice the configured window, up to 0.5 Da) precursor and fragment windows (the configured ones if wider) so the error is measured and not censored, takes the offset (median) and the spread (robust standard deviation, 1.4826 * MAD) of the signed mass errors of its confident PSMs; the main search then uses the fragment tolerance |median| + k sigma (calibration:sigma_factor k) within [calibration:min_fragment_tolerance, the configured tolerance], and the precursor window [median - k sigma, median + k sigma] only with calibration:precursor_sigma_factor k > 0 (by default the precursor errors are measured and reported, the configured window kept): the configured tolerances are the widest windows searched. The pass takes its spectra per tenth of the run; a window that covers less than 98 % of the calibration PSMs (precursor; heavy tails or a mass offset that changes over the run) or 95 % of their matched fragment peaks (fragment) is not trusted, and the configured tolerance is kept with a warning. The fragment index is not rebuilt, only the query-time tolerances change. With too few PSMs (calibration:min_psms) the configured tolerances are used. 'false' searches with the configured tolerances as given.

name: calibration:subset_ratio
description: Fraction of spectra (by TIC, highest first) used for the calibration pass (0.0-1.0).

name: calibration:min_psms
description: Minimum number of confident PSMs required for calibration. If fewer are found, calibration is skipped and the user-configured tolerances are used.

name: calibration:sigma_factor
description: Half-width of the calibrated fragment tolerance in robust standard deviations (1.4826 * MAD) of the signed errors of the matched fragment peaks of the calibration PSMs: |median| + k sigma. 4 covers practically all correct matches of a normal error distribution.

name: calibration:precursor_sigma_factor
description: Half-width of the calibrated precursor window in robust standard deviations of the precursor errors of the calibration PSMs, around their median (asymmetric about zero when the run has an offset). 0 keeps the configured precursor window and only measures and reports the errors: precursor yields are flat from 5 to 50 ppm, and a tightened precursor window cost identifications on every Orbitrap HCD set of the benchmark (heavy tails), while the fragment window gains. A value such as 4 tightens it, within calibration:min_precursor_tolerance and the configured window, when the window covers 98 % of the calibration PSMs.

name: calibration:min_precursor_tolerance
description: Smallest calibrated precursor tolerance per side, in precursor:mass_tolerance_unit (0: 2.5 ppm or 0.005 Da). The calibrated window never exceeds the configured one.

name: calibration:min_fragment_tolerance
description: Smallest calibrated fragment tolerance, in fragment:mass_tolerance_unit (0: 10 ppm or 0.02 Da; 5 ppm or 0.01 Da with calibration:recalibrate). The calibrated tolerance never exceeds the configured one.

name: calibration:recalibrate
description: Correct the m/z of the spectra by the mass errors the calibration pass measures, before the main search: 'offset' subtracts the median error, 'linear' a line in m/z fitted to the errors (precursor errors against the precursor m/z, fragment errors against the fragment m/z), each per retention-time chunk (calibration:recalibrate_rt_chunks) and interpolated between the chunks. The precursor m/z and the fragment peaks of the searched MS2 spectra are corrected in place (the candidate retrieval, the scoring and the PSMs' mass errors use the corrected values; a PeakMap passed to the library is corrected too); the PSMs report the observed precursor m/z and their fragment annotations the observed peak m/z. The windows are then derived from the residual errors, with a fragment floor of 5 ppm (0.01 Da) unless calibration:min_fragment_tolerance is set. The co-isolated precursors of a chimeric search, from the same survey scans, are corrected by the precursor model. 'none' measures only.

name: calibration:recalibrate_rt_chunks
description: Retention-time chunks of the recalibration models (calibration:recalibrate): the calibration PSMs are split in acquisition order into this many groups of equal size (fewer when a group would hold less than calibration:min_psms PSMs), one model each, interpolated between the groups' median retention times. 1: one model for the run; 10 follows an offset that changes over the run (the pass samples each tenth of it).

name: database:chunk_size
description: Split the protein database into chunks of at most this many proteins for fragment index building. 0 = disabled (load entire database at once). Enable for very large databases (e.g. MHC-II immunopeptidomics with variants) that exceed available memory. Each chunk builds its own fragment index; results are merged across chunks before post-processing. Calibration (when enabled) runs on a strided, size-bounded sample of the full decoy-augmented database — sample size is tied to chunk_size so calibration memory respects the same budget as main-search chunks. In multi-file mode (-in a.mzML b.mzML), the chunk-major path builds each chunk's fragment index once and scores all files against it before moving to the next chunk. Note that chunk_size bounds only the fragment-index memory: the chunk-major schedule holds ALL input files' preprocessed MS2 spectra in memory for the whole search, so budget for their sum as well, or split very large cohorts across separate ProSE invocations.

name: chimeric:enabled
description: Also identify precursors co-isolated with the selected one (after the andes chimeric cascade). The survey scan of each MS2 spectrum is searched for isotope envelopes in its isolation window that fit averagine (needs centroided MS1 spectra in the input and isolation windows on the precursors). After the search, the peaks the best hit of the spectrum explains are removed, and the rest is searched for each co-isolated precursor in turn, at its m/z and charge; the best hit of each removes the peaks it explains before the next is searched. The best hit's peptide is not a hit of a co-isolated precursor, and a co-isolated precursor whose best hit repeats a PSM of the spectrum (same peptide and charge) is dropped. These PSMs get the spectrum reference of their spectrum and the PSM meta value 'chimeric_rank' 2 (the others 1). Not with database:chunk_size > 0.

name: chimeric:max_coisolated
description: At most this many co-isolated precursors per spectrum, the most intense first.

name: chimeric:max_kl
description: Largest Kullback-Leibler divergence of an isotope envelope in the survey scan from averagine (first four isotope peaks) to accept it as a co-isolated precursor.

name: chimeric:top_hits
description: At most this many hits of a co-isolated precursor are reported (and at most report:top_hits). Each takes about as much memory as a hit of a spectrum.

name: chimeric:mz_tolerance
description: Tolerance (ppm) for the m/z of the isotope peaks in the survey scan.
